## `things-cli` v0.9.0 — edits confirm what happened

`things edit` and `things project edit` used to exit 0 with no output, so an agent had to run `things show` to learn whether the change had landed. They now wait for Things to record the write and print the item, in the same form as `things show`, so one call does both. How long the CLI waits for that confirmation can now be configured. Two behaviour changes, below.

### Behaviour changes

- **`edit` and `project edit` print the edited item.** The output is the same as `things show` for that item, plain or `--json`. Anything that expected these commands to print nothing needs updating. (#280)
- **An edit Things drops now fails.** The CLI waits for the item's modification date to change and exits non-zero with `edit did not apply: …` if it never does. Before, a dropped edit reported success. An edit that only re-sets values the item already has is caught before the wait when it uses `--title`, `--notes`, `--tags`, `--add-tags` or a `--deadline` date. Any other flag, `--when` included, still waits and reports the same error, because Things does not record a no-op as a change. The error says to check with `things show <uuid>` before retrying. (#280)

### Also

- `--no-verify` and `--duplicate` edits print a line saying the edit was sent but not confirmed, with `"confirmed": false` and a `reason` under `--json`, rather than printing nothing. (#280)
- **The read-back wait is configurable**, with `--verify-timeout` or the `verify_timeout` config key, and defaults to 5s. It applies to every write that is read back: `complete`, `cancel`, `edit`, `project edit`, `import` and `tag add`. In v0.8.0, `complete`, `cancel`, `import` and `tag add` waited 10s before reporting a change as not applied; they now give up after 5s unless configured otherwise. (#281)
- The bundled skill tells agents that exit 0 with the item printed means the edit is confirmed, and to put several changes to one item in a single `edit`. Run `things skill install` after upgrading. (#280, #281)

### Requirements

macOS with Things3 installed. Binaries for Apple Silicon (`darwin_arm64`) and Intel (`darwin_amd64`).
